data.narrative:
XMOS is a Growth-stage semiconductor chip company that has raised £200M+ to date. The valuation exercise draws on a universe of 12 same-sector peers (3 public: ALAB, NVDA, AMD; 8 private including Cerebras, Credo Semiconductor, and SambaNova Systems), though narrow-filter peer matching proved insufficient for direct comparison.

Stage-progression analysis is the primary applicable method. Using total capital raised (£200M) as a proxy baseline and applying a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical of Growth-stage advancement yields £240M. Public semiconductor comps trade at a median P/S of 20.5x, but this anchor cannot be deployed absent disclosed revenue figures—standard for private companies in this sector.

The triangulated valuation range spans £204M (floor, conservative) to £276M (ceiling, optimistic), with £240M as the central estimate. This range reflects the single-method limitation: only stage-progression yielded a quantifiable result. Key uncertainties include the absence of comparable Growth-stage semiconductor peers at similar valuation tiers and lack of revenue visibility, both of which constrain triangulation depth. The analysis would strengthen materially with peer revenue disclosure or additional Growth-stage private semiconductor comparables.
